maiko.title: "Maiko"
maiko.description: Tasked with creating a sculpture centered on clothing, I drew inspiration from my deep admiration for Japanese culture and decided to model a Maiko. I conducted extensive research into the distinctions between Maiko and Geisha, the history of the Shamisen, and the intricate technique of tying the Neo knot.

monophobia.title: "Monophobia"
monophobia.description: This is a deeply personal work. At the time of its creation, I believed I was experiencing monophobia (the fear of being alone), though I later learned this was a manifestation of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). This sculpture was exhibited at KunstWerk in Potsdam, Germany.

gameworld.title: "Gameworld"
gameworld.description: This work is a love letter to my interest in computing and gaming. I gathered a vast collection of vintage electronic components—primarily from servers—and began experimenting with their forms. I eventually settled on this mech-inspired figure.

upsidedown.title: "Upside Down"
upsidedown.description: I was working on this sculpture when the first wave of COVID-19 arrived. After the school was shut down, leaving the piece unfinished, I decided to embrace this incompleteness as the central concept. The final touch was turning the sculpture upside down—a reflection of how our world had been upended during those times.

weldybee.title: "Weldybee"
weldybee.description: Created as the culmination of a welding course, this sculpture is fabricated from steel. While scavenging in a scrapyard, I discovered a vintage car spring and realized it would serve as an excellent abdomen for a bee; from there, the rest is history.

heart.title: "Süda"
heart.description: I participated in a sculpture contest for a hospital in Viljandi. The brief required the piece to be themed around health and medicine. The sculpture was designed to be cast in bronze and stand approximately 3 meters tall. It featured LED lights representing the veins surrounding the heart, with an integrated LED wall positioned inside the heart itself. Although the work didn't win, it was voted into second place by the general public.

girl_relief.title: "Girl low relief"
girl_relief.description: An anatomical study of the female head, realized as a low-relief sculpture.
girl_relief.alt: Low relief sculpture of a girl

fractals.title: "My Future Space"
fractals.description: For my Bachelor's thesis project, I envisioned a future scenario where humanity has migrated to the mesosphere due to climate change, living on gigantic, floating sculptural objects. What started as a simple 3D sculpture and architectural visualization project has evolved into a massive worldbuilding endeavor.

about_page.intro1: For me, art is quite a broad concept. Probably because I'm young and I can absorb it all - different materials, colours and technologies. However, I tend to lean more towards newer art methods, the most exciting of which is 3D. For me, this form of visual expression offers the most freedom and surprising results.
about_page.intro2: I have a rather 'weird' approach to generating ideas - new and exciting ideas that pop into my head and stay there for quite a long time before they start to form into something more concrete. I don't draw or write anything anywhere, but I think intensely and finally decide that now is the time to get something done. This can happen spontaneously or by forcing myself. The work is usually slow, I like to let it settle for a couple of months or more and then come back again.
about_page.intro3: I find ideas in different places but the main source is still the internet. That's where there's the most information and where cultures, subcultures and countercultures evolve rapidly. I'm most into visually stricking themes and architecture but I'm also interested in different cultures. Lately, I have started to look more closely at different political and geopolitical issues, the human psyche, mental disorders and how this gives rise to different subcultures and/or countercultures.

fractals_page.title: PROJECT FRACTALS
fractals_page.desc1: This worldbuilding project started out as a Bachelor's thesis project titled <1>{{link1_text}}</1>. I wanted to envision a future space scenario where humanity, due to climate change, has migrated to the mesosphere, living on gigantic floating sculptural objects. The capsules within these objects serve as individual living quarters, inspired by shapes from nature. In addition to the capsules, there is also a communal area where everyone gets to socialize. My design process involved extensive research, drawing inspiration from various sources including architectural marvels in Asia, science fiction literature, and film classics from the 60’s to the modern age big blockbuster spectacles.
fractals_page.desc2: You can find the full thesis <1>{{link2_text}}</1> in Estonian, and I want to thank Merille Hommik for being an amazing mentor throughout this bachelor’s project.
fractals_page.desc3: Updates on this project are slow due to my time being taken up by other projects and life changes.

films_page.title: MY FAVOURITE FILMS, SERIES, DOCUMENTARIES AND ANIME
films_page.imdb_link: If you're interested, you can check out my ratings for films & series <1>here</1>. It's far from complete though, I'm updating it periodically.

br.title: Blade Runner - 1982
br.desc: - The stunning world of Philip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? created on film in fantastic detail.

br2049.title: Blade Runner 2049 - 2017
br2049.desc: - One of the best film sequels ever made. It’s distinctly Blade Runner, yet it’s different enough in its tonality and direction to stand on it's own two feet.

alien.title: Alien - 1979
alien.desc: - Holds up incredibly well in its horror elements. Spectacular set design and atmosphere.

space_odyssey.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey - 1968
space_odyssey.desc: - It’s so good that it convinced a certain group of people that the Earth is flat. Enough said.

dune.title: Dune part 1 & 2 - 2021/2024
dune.desc: - The unfilmable book capsured on film by one of the best directors of our time. CINEMA!

lotr.title: LOTR Trilogy - 2001/2002/2003
lotr.desc: - The gold standard of worldbuilding, made into three films by an incredibly passionate group of people. It’s just magical.

arrival.title: Arrival - 2016
arrival.desc: - A fantastic take on the sci-fi genre. Great acting and directing.

whiplash.title: Whiplash - 2014
whiplash.desc: - Proves that you don’t need a big budget to make an amazing film. The corrosive and convoluted relationship between a student who longs for his teacher’s praise is really chilling and hits home.

joker.title: Joker - 2019
joker.desc: - A very different take on a classic Batman villain. In a time of mental health crisis—either because people are increasingly lonely or because some think it’s ‘cool’—Joker’s relevance is only bound to increase.

y1917.desc: - Spectacular cinematography disguised as a war film that is just brutal.

pirates.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl - 2003
pirates.desc: - Pirates used to be cartoony and something you’d scare kids with, but not after this film. It’s an absolute gem that still holds up incredibly well visually, and Johnny Depp is just brilliant.

oppenheimer.title: Oppenheimer - 2023
oppenheimer.desc: - Written like an action flick, but it’s just some guys in a room talking and a big explosion at the halfway mark. And yet it managed to keep me on the edge of my seat for the full runtime. It’s also got some interesting back-and-forth between the black-and-white and color shots—one from Strauss’s POV and the other from Oppenheimer’s, respectively. I wish I’d had the chance to see it in IMAX.

bb.title: Breaking Bad - 2008 - 2013
bb.desc: - A couple of filler episodes a side, it's ability to deliver 8+/10 so consistently over such a long runtime is impressive.

got.title: Game of Thrones - 2011 - 2019
got.desc: - As long as you don't watch the last two seasons, it's solid television with complex characters and interesting plotlines.

andor.title: Andor - 2022- 2025
andor.desc: - Surprisingly deep narrative for Star Wars. It's also pretty relevant in today's world.

mr_robot.title: Mr. Robot - 2015 - 2019
mr_robot.desc: - My personal favourite series. Every twist and turn is carefully thought out. It’s even better on a rewatch, especially Season 1.

chernobyl.title: Chernobyl - 2019
chernobyl.desc: - One of the best miniseries ever made. Captures the human condition of living in the Soviet Union quite well.

house.title: House M.D. - 2004 - 2012
house.desc: - A medical drama made fun by a flawed, hilarious, and witty doctor.

aib.title: Alice in Borderland - 2020 - 2025
aib.desc: - Stellar first two seasons; the third falls flat. Overall, very engaging, fun, and mindfucky.

clarkson.title: Clarkson's Farm - 2021 - ?
clarkson.desc: - A guy who drove cars for a living now drives tractors for a living. Clarkson’s Farm is hilarious, emotional, educational, and important.

shogun.title: Shogun - 2024 - 2026
shogun.desc: - A classic tale, masterfully remade. Perfectly showcases the brutality and beauty of Edo-era Japan.

andriivka.title: 2000 Meters to Andriivka - 2026
andriivka.desc: - A very raw and gut-wrenching look at the incremental steps to retake the strategic village of Andriivka. It shows the reality of everyday life on the front lines and how modern war changes a man.

sinikollane.title: Sinikollane - 2025
sinikollane.desc: - This story follows an Estonian volunteer medic Erko Laidinen and his family for many months, showing that the effects of war are just as damning for the ones staying at home as they are for the ones fighting.

into_the_void.title: Into the Void: Putin's Foreign Fighters - 2026
into_the_void.desc: - How Russia recruits citizens from the Global South for it's illegal war in Ukraine.

initial_d.title: Initial D - 1998 - 2014
initial_d.desc: - The anime that sparked my interest in cars. An absolute classic. I daydream about making my own animated car drift battle. Hopefully, someday I can realize that dream.

edgerunners.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners - 2022 - ?
edgerunners.desc: - If you like Cyberpunk 2077, you will love this anime. This stayed with me for a long time.

cp2077.title: Cyberpunk 2077 - 2020/2023
cp2077.desc: - One of the coolest video game worlds ever. Everything is rooted in reality, and everything has a purpose. Combat is incredibly fun and varied. A kickass soundtrack. The narrative uses the worldbuilding exceptionally well, and it’s not just a story about punks fighting the system or a gun-for-hire climbing the criminal underworld ladder. Cyberpunk 2077’s main quest is far more philosophical, drawing heavily from existentialism and posthumanism. At its core, it’s a story about identity, weaving that theme through every part of the game. The length of the main quest is also pretty spot on. It’s sharp and to the point — all killer, no filler. The quests have some decision-making that ripples outward, though less so than The Witcher 3, but the production value is also higher. The characters are excellent. - 9/10

witcher3.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - 2015/2016
witcher3.desc: - This game showed everyone (and Bethesda) that vast open-world games can have an abundance of complex stories and well-written characters. The combat is by far the weakest link, but it’s by no means bad, and eventually becomes fun. Both main and side quests offer a decent amount of decision-making, with consequences that appear later down the line. Gwent was so good that CDPR ended up making a separate game just for it. The soundtrack is just lovely. - 8/10
